craft_notes: SEAL of the work: yielding; potsherd names itself (literal kept, metaphor in C1). Speaker/yamaka opens held per BOUNDARY. REJECTED OPTIONS (with killers): (a) resolving speaker -> killed held-open. (b) naming yamaka words -> killed unidentified. (c) closing with triumph -> killed: yielding is the close. Read aloud: MAY-i BE-con-QUERED — BY-which OTH-er PO-et, WITH-ya-ma-kas — … TO-him I-POUR wa-ter IN a POT-sherd. Abhinavagupta frame: rasa shifting śṛṅgāra → vīra/adbhuta — lover's voice yielding to poet's; sthāyibhāva (love) resolving into camatkāra (wonder at craft); seal names its own vessel.

lines: May I be conquered — by which other poet, with yamakas —
to him I pour water in a potsherd.
l4.sanskrit_cite: jīyeya yena kavinā yamakaiḥ pareṇa tasmai vaheyam udakaṃ ghaṭakarpareṇa

c1_essence: The rasa shifts from śṛṅgāra to vira/adbhuta: love and landscape are framed by the poet's skill, not by love alone. Clouds thundering make travelers long; sorrow grows, endless. Lovers honor the love-festival; cloud-arrival, dear friend, they bring. Then the tribute: may I be conquered by which poet, by yamakas; to him I pour water in ghaṭakarpara. The sthāyibhāva (love) resolves into the poet's own delight (camatkāra) at his craft. The potsherd is both vessel and namesake — the potsherd names itself at its close.
reads_against.c1_rasa: vira/adbhuta (heroic skill + wonder at craft), resolving from śṛṅgāra
